newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline called up on possible Unocal strike.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline called up on possible Unocal strike.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline was called higher on a threat by workers at four Unocal refineries in California to go on strike, while crude was called steady despite being driven up on overnight trading.
"There could have been a big player that spiked it (crude) up last night because volume was pretty good for ACCESS," said a New York crude dealer.
Crude was called steady to five cents lower while heating oil and gasoline were called up 0.25 to 0.50 cent a gallon.
May crude rose 37 cents to $22.22 a barrel on ACCESS after falling back to $21.83, off three cents.

"Sometimes guys (who are long) goose up the market overnight to make crude look better. Although the volume was a little better on ACCESS it wasn't that much better to look strange," said another New York crude trader.

Meanwhile, workers at at four Unocal Corp refineries in California threatened to go on a three-day strike soon citing disagreement with Unocal over how to close out its contract before Tosco Corp takes over the refineries March 31.
"Sometimes problems on the West Coast can spill over onto the Merc since there could be situations where the arb starts makes sense," said Refco Inc vice president Victor Yu.
Dealers said if prices rise enough on the West Coast due to supply tightening it could draw gasoline from the East Coast.
On Thursday, May crude ended up three cents at $21.85 a barrel. April gasoline settled off 0.38 cent a gallon at 67.58 cents while April heating oil ended off 0.35 cent at 55.94 cents a gallon.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
